s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status, fever, flaccid paralysis, and respiratory failure with evidence of disseminated infection and multi-organ involvement
key_facts: Patient is around 60 years old
Patient lives in a rural area in the southeastern US
Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy
Patient has a history of alcohol use disorder
Patient has a recent diagnosis of hyper-IgE syndrome
Patient was taking oral prednisone before admission
Patient presented with fever
Patient has respiratory failure with lower lobe nodules and a left lower lobe infiltrate
Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Aspergillus fumigatus, Candida spp, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Autopsy findings showed disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis
Multiple organ involvement including lungs, liver, pancreas, colon, appendix, and kidneys

shortlist.label: Strongyloidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Flaccid paralysis and respiratory failure are consistent with strongyloidiasis

shortlist.label: Toxocariasis
shortlist.why_kept: Eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate and larval sections in autopsy findings

shortlist.label: Cysticercosis
shortlist.why_kept: Flaccid paralysis and altered mental status are consistent with cysticercosis

shortlist.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Flaccid paralysis and respiratory failure are consistent with Guillain-Barré syndrome

shortlist.label: Porphyric neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of porphyria with polyneuropathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, flaccid paralysis, and respiratory distress, combined with the autopsy findings of eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrates and larval sections in the eyes, is most consistent with strongyloidiasis, particularly given the patient's immunocompromised state due to hyper-IgE syndrome and prednisone use.

rejected.label: Disseminated aspergillosis
rejected.why: While aspergillosis is present, it does not fully explain the flaccid paralysis and eosinophil-rich infiltrates.

rejected.label: Disseminated candidiasis
rejected.why: Candidiasis is also present but does not account for the larval sections found in the eyes.

rejected.label: Toxocariasis
rejected.why: Toxocariasis typically presents with visceral larva migrans or ocular larva migrans, but the patient's systemic symptoms and autopsy findings are more suggestive of strongyloidiasis.

rejected.label: Cysticercosis
rejected.why: Cysticercosis could explain some findings, but the presence of larval sections in the eyes and the patient's immunocompromised state point more towards strongyloidiasis.

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
rejected.why: Pseudomonas infection is present but does not explain the parasitic findings.

rejected.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
rejected.why: Guillain-Barré syndrome could explain the flaccid paralysis but not the parasitic findings or the eosinophil-rich infiltrates.

rejected.label: Porphyric neuropathy
rejected.why: Porphyric neuropathy is part of the patient's history but does not account for the acute presentation or the parasitic findings.
